description: At its 2026-09-10 meeting the ECB raised its three key rates by 25bp, taking the deposit rate from 2.25% to 2.5% -- its SECOND hike since the US-Iran war began (the first was 2026-06-11). The move followed euro-area August inflation at 3.3% YoY (energy inflation 14.3%) and was WIDELY EXPECTED going in, so it confirms rather than surprises. Growth forecasts were upgraded (2026: 0.9%, 2027: 1.4%) while the inflation path was pushed higher for 2027/2028 (2.5% / 2.1%). This corroborates cat_20260617_fed_hawkish_pivot and the same Iran/Hormuz energy-shock driver (cat_20260817_hormuz_reescalation): three major central banks (Fed, ECB, and a BoJ decision due 2026-09-17/18) are now hiking in the same window, a synchronized-tightening regime the market had not priced as of mid-2026.

strength_anchors.note: Rubric total 55 (str_02+str_04+str_05); a single 25bp move that was already priced is not a magnitude or surprise event, but a decided, corroborated, persistent-rate change from an official primary source outranks a market-structure bill and sits just below a climate supply shock. Adjusted +1 to sit strictly between the two anchors.

user_notes: Registrado en el scan del 2026-09-14 disparado por la pregunta del usuario sobre el cambio de tipos de interes. No es un evento aislado: Fed (decision 15-16/09, mercado pricing 85-90% de subida tras el CPI del 11/09), ECB (ya subida, 10/09) y BoJ (decision 17-18/09, 62% de subida priced) se mueven en la MISMA ventana por el MISMO driver -- el shock energetico Iran/Hormuz. sector_impact adverse en grid_infrastructure_utilities es DIRECTO sobre una posicion abierta (IQQH.DE): mayor coste de capital para el buildout de red, corroborado por la rebaja de outlook de Fitch a utilities el mismo mes (ver refresh de struct_energy_transition_grid). gold_physical adverse es el canal de tipo real, distinto del canal de acumulacion de bancos centrales (struct_cb_gold_accumulation), que sigue neto comprador.

review_log.evidence: Deposit rate 2.50% after the 2026-09-10 hike; Lagarde says the energy-driven inflation shock lasts longer than expected, Schnabel says further hikes will likely be needed; markets and most economists expect a hold on 2026-10-29 and a hike in December. September euro-area PMI price pressures sharpest in four months.
